ADVISOR; 09/2026'. Claim C77 files it under the Yorkville Ives build, but no opened source links it to Yorkville Ives (New Jersey); a web search finds only an unrelated Innovation X Advisors in Rockville, MD. As written, the colon list reads as complete and hides an outside advisory role taken about two months after 'I needed to simplify' and '110% focused'. Relatedly, 'Most of what followed belongs to the new firm' overstates IVAI: per IFR (S33) Yorkville Ives owns 49.9% of the adviser (the Leathers hold 50%), and FINRA lists his Ives Ultra Fund chairmanship (09/2026) as an outside business activity. findings.acceptance_test: (a) The FINRA sentence either names the September 2026 Innovation X Global Opportunities advisory role (attributed to FINRA, dated, no motive guessed) or cites an opened source showing it is part of Yorkville Ives; the list no longer reads as complete if it is not. (b) 'Most of what followed belongs to the new firm' is reworded to match the sources, e.g. a fund whose adviser Yorkville Ives owns 49.9% of, which FINRA lists among his outside activities. (c) The 'Leaving Eightco was a real cut...' paragraph and the Why-not-Type-3 forward test still read correctly with the extra role included. (d) C77's claim text and inference, and C128's inference, are corrected to match, with no unsourced classification.

findings.passage: In launch week he spoke in possibilities.
findings.problem: The Seven-over-Three discriminator (C37, C158) rests on his self-reported motives in friendly or promotional interviews and on cost-reframes ('undervalued asset', 'third inning') that a chairman and sell-side analyst would also make. The article concedes that roles and repairs do not discriminate and that 'The call is close.' It also omits Three-leaning results language from the same launch interview it cites. Business Insider (S06), July 15, 2026: 'You just have to convince people, you have to show them the results.' Fortune (S05) narrates that 'he knows the proof will be in the pudding.' The page's forward test says the Three reading gains if he measures the build 'by results', but it does not report that he already framed the launch that way. With the rival not failing any specific, sourced discriminator, the type argument meets the standard's Enneagram 7-8 description, not the 8 the release gate requires.
findings.acceptance_test: (a) The launch-week paragraph or the Why-not-Type-3 section reports 'you have to show them the results' (BI, July 15, 2026) and weighs it, and the forward test is restated so the existing evidence does not already half-satisfy it. (b) The Seven lead adds at least one opened, dated observation that the Three reading does not predict. Examples: a first-person or named-testimony account of why he left research for Synchronoss in 2016 and came back; or a choice where novelty or freedom cost him recognition or status. Place it beside the discriminator and record it in the evidence inventory. (c) If research finds no such observation, the honest outcome is status insufficient_evidence with those research tasks. Releasing the profile as a medium-confidence Seven whose rival never fails a test is not acceptable.

findings.passage: The violations were of internal-controls and books-and-records rules.
findings.problem: The SEC order (S10) finds that Ives violated Section 13(b)(5) and Rule 13b2-1 (internal controls and falsified records).
